audit_boundary: Read-only currentness and source-identity revalidation. This does not establish legal, clinical, security, certification, implementation or product-compliance conclusions.
method: Re-opened or searched the six authoritative primary-source identities on 2026-08-24. Recorded only current publication identity, version/date signals and the narrow proposition boundary visible in the authority's own current material.

sources.authority: Office of the Privacy Commissioner New Zealand
sources.current_signal: The current HIPC page states that Amendment No 2 reflects IPP3A and that the amended Code is in force from 1 May 2026.
sources.boundary: The source establishes the current privacy-code text and notice context; it does not decide Oblivion applicability, exceptions, data classification or implementation design.

sources.authority: Health New Zealand / Health Information Standards Organisation
sources.current_signal: The current Health New Zealand page still lists HISO 10029:2022 and separately lists 2025 supplier guidance; the page reports a 21 May 2026 update.
sources.boundary: The framework supplies a security-control context only. It does not prove system scope, conformity, certification, risk acceptance or that a specific Oblivion control is mandatory.

sources.current_signal: The current published NZ Base Implementation Guide identifies release 3.1.0 as active from 24 July 2026 and describes reusable New Zealand FHIR artefacts.
sources.boundary: NZ Base does not itself define complete conformance requirements or require particular resources, profiles, extensions or interactions for Oblivion.

sources.current_signal: The current Ministry page states that NZS 8134:2021 has applied since 28 February 2022, uses a modular certification framework and was updated on 11 February 2026.
sources.boundary: Applicability is service- and certification-scope dependent; the page does not certify a provider or prescribe a specific Oblivion workflow or control.

sources.authority: Health and Disability Commissioner New Zealand
sources.current_signal: The current HDC page continues to publish the full Code, including Right 4 service-quality duties and Right 7 informed-choice, presumed-competence, consent and refusal provisions.
sources.boundary: The Code provides rights and provider-duty context; actual authority, competence, exceptions and product workflow design require case-specific specialist decisions.

sources.current_signal: The current WorkSafe guidance continues to define notifiable events as specified work-related deaths, injuries or illnesses, or incidents, with prompt notification, site-preservation and record obligations for serious events.
sources.boundary: The guidance does not prescribe Oblivion's classifier, lifecycle, RBAC, Site-scope or evidence model, and work-relatedness remains a factual and specialist decision.

completion_credit: Source-identity/currentness gate only. No runtime, legal-assurance, clinical-assurance, security-assurance, feature, module or remediation credit is awarded.
